what: Israel and Lebanon sign framework agreement after US-brokered talks

clean_source_blocks.text: Israel and Lebanon have signed a framework agreement in Washington after days of negotiations brokered by the US. The deal, details of which remain unclear, is something of a victory for the Trump administration, which is itself embroiled in complex negotiations with Iran following the extension of a ceasefire between the two. Iran - Hezbollah's primary foreign backer - has repeatedly called for Lebanon to form part of any negotiations with the US. The agreement "begins to put in place a framework for lasting peace and security," US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Friday. "That's what these two nations deserve," he said, calling it a "first step". Previous ceasefires between Israel and Hezbollah have still seen near-daily cross-border strikes, with both sides accusing each other of violating the agreement.
Previous ceasefires between Israel and Hezbollah have still seen near-daily cross-border strikes

Washington: Lebanon and Israel have signed a US-brokered framework agreement following several days of negotiations in Washington, marking what American officials described as an initial step towards peace. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the two sides had reached the agreement after talks in the US capital, adding that negotiators had taken "an important step towards achieving peace between Lebanon and Israel", while cautioning that "there is still a long way to go". Lebanese Ambassador to the United States Nada Moawad described the signing as "a first step towards restoring Lebanon's sovereignty". No further details of the framework agreement were immediately released. ---

In a video statement issued after the signing, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu touted that the deal would allow Israel to remain in the buffer zone it created in southern Lebanon. It would also establish two pilot zones, one located south of the Litani River and the other to the north of it, Netanyahu said. Lebanon was dragged back into war on March 2 when Hezbollah fired at Israel in solidarity with its patron, Iran. Israel responded with a wave of airstrikes and a ground operation in southern Lebanon that killed more than 4,000 Lebanese and displaced over 1.2 million others. More than 30 Israelis have died in the conflict, mostly soldiers. The fighting between Israel and the Iran-backed group has threatened to derail a US-Iran framework agreement calling for an end to military operations “on all fronts, including Lebanon.”

Israel and Lebanon have signed a framework agreement in Washington after days of negotiations brokered by the US.

The deal, details of which remain unclear, is something of a victory for the Trump administration, which is itself embroiled in complex negotiations with Iran following the extension of a ceasefire between the two.

Iran - Hezbollah's primary foreign backer - has repeatedly called for Lebanon to form part of any negotiations with the US.

The agreement "begins to put in place a framework for lasting peace and security," US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Friday. "That's what these two nations deserve," he said, calling it a "first step".

Previous ceasefires between Israel and Hezbollah have still seen near-daily cross-border strikes, with both sides accusing each other of violating the agreement.

Washington has feared that continuing tensions between Israel and Lebanon could undermine the US peace deal with Iran, which holds a commitment to end fighting on "all fronts", including Lebanon.

Over the course of several months, repeated Israeli strikes on targets in southern Lebanon threatened to derail efforts to settle the conflict in the Middle East.

US President Donald Trump on one occasion held a terse phone call with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, in which he reportedly uttered an expletive. He also publicly criticized Netanyahu and Israeli conduct in the conflict  on several occasions.

The Israel-Lebanon deal, however, could be tenuous. Hezbollah is not a party to Friday's agreement, and it is unclear whether it will agree to withdraw its fighters from the South Litani area in southern Lebanon.

While Trump has insisted that Israel has a right to defend itself from Hezbollah rocket strikes on its territories,  he has also claimed he can "control Israel from attacking Lebanon."

"They have a lot of respect for me," Trump told Axios in an interview last week. "They do as I say."

Lebanon was drawn into the war between the US and Israel and Iran on 2 March, when Hezbollah launched rockets into Israel in retaliation for an Israeli strike that killed Iran's supreme leader. Israel responded with an air campaign across Lebanon and a ground invasion in the south.

A US-brokered ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon on 16 April failed to stop the fighting.

WASHINGTON — A US-brokered agreement on Friday sets the stage for Israel to transfer control of two areas in southern Lebanon to the Lebanese military.

payload.title: Israel ja Libanon allekirjoittivat Yhdysvaltain välittämän puitesopimuksen
payload.summary: Israel ja Libanon ovat allekirjoittaneet Washingtonissa puitesopimuksen useita päiviä kestäneiden Yhdysvaltain välittämien neuvottelujen jälkeen. Sopimuksen yksityiskohdat ovat vielä epäselviä, ja osapuolet sekä yhdysvaltalaisviranomaiset kuvaavat sitä vasta ensimmäiseksi askeleeksi.
payload.content:
Israel ja Libanon ovat allekirjoittaneet Washingtonissa puitesopimuksen useita päiviä kestäneiden Yhdysvaltain välittämien neuvottelujen jälkeen. Sopimuksen tarkkaa sisältöä ei ole julkistettu, mutta Yhdysvaltain ulkoministeri Marco Rubio kuvasi sitä ensimmäiseksi askeleeksi kohti rauhaa ja turvallisuutta kahden maan välillä.

## Sopimuksen yksityiskohdat yhä avoinna

Rubion mukaan sopimus alkaa luoda kehystä pysyvälle rauhalle ja turvallisuudelle. Hän sanoi neuvottelijoiden ottaneen tärkeän askeleen kohti rauhaa Israelin ja Libanonin välillä, mutta varoitti samalla, että edessä on vielä pitkä tie.

Libanonin Yhdysvaltain-suurlähettiläs Nada Moawad kuvasi allekirjoitusta ensimmäiseksi askeleeksi Libanonin suvereniteetin palauttamisessa. Sopimuksesta ei kuitenkaan annettu heti tarkempia tietoja, mikä jättää avoimeksi, mitä osapuolet ovat käytännössä sitoutuneet tekemään ja millä aikataululla.

Israelin pääministeri Benjamin Netanyahu sanoi allekirjoituksen jälkeen julkaistussa videolausunnossa, että sopimus mahdollistaisi Israelin pysymisen sen Etelä-Libanoniin perustamalla puskurivyöhykkeellä. Hänen mukaansa sopimus loisi myös kaksi pilottialuetta, joista toinen sijaitsisi Litani-joen eteläpuolella ja toinen sen pohjoispuolella.

## Taustalla Israelin ja Hizbollahin sota

Puitesopimus syntyy tilanteessa, jossa aiemmat tulitauot Israelin ja Hizbollahin välillä eivät ole lopettaneet väkivaltaa rajaseudulla. Tulitauoista huolimatta alueella on nähty lähes päivittäisiä iskuja rajan yli, ja osapuolet ovat syyttäneet toisiaan sopimusten rikkomisesta.

Libanon ajautui uudelleen sotaan 2. maaliskuuta, kun Hizbollah ampui Israeliin osoittaakseen tukea Iranille. Israel vastasi ilmaiskuilla ja maaoperaatiolla Etelä-Libanonissa. Taisteluissa on kuollut yli 4 000 libanonilaista ja yli 1,2 miljoonaa ihmistä on joutunut lähtemään kodeistaan. Israelilaisia on kuollut yli 30, pääosin sotilaita.

Neuvottelut liittyvät myös laajempaan alueelliseen asetelmaan. Iran on Hizbollahin tärkein ulkomainen tukija ja on vaatinut Libanonin aseman huomioimista Yhdysvaltain kanssa käytävissä neuvotteluissa. Israelin ja Iranin tukeman Hizbollahin välinen taistelu on uhannut vaikeuttaa Yhdysvaltain ja Iranin välistä kehystä, jonka tavoitteena olisi sotatoimien lopettaminen kaikilla rintamilla, myös Libanonissa.

Washington: Lebanon and Israel have signed a US-brokered framework agreement following several days of negotiations in Washington, marking what American officials described as an initial step towards peace. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the two sides had reached the agreement after talks in the US capital, adding that negotiators had taken "an important step towards achieving peace between Lebanon and Israel", while cautioning that "there is still a long way to go". Lebanese Ambassador to the United States Nada Moawad described the signing as "a first step towards restoring Lebanon's sovereignty". No further details of the framework agreement were immediately released. ---

In a video statement issued after the signing, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu touted that the deal would allow Israel to remain in the buffer zone it created in southern Lebanon. It would also establish two pilot zones, one located south of the Litani River and the other to the north of it, Netanyahu said. Lebanon was dragged back into war on March 2 when Hezbollah fired at Israel in solidarity with its patron, Iran. Israel responded with a wave of airstrikes and a ground operation in southern Lebanon that killed more than 4,000 Lebanese and displaced over 1.2 million others. More than 30 Israelis have died in the conflict, mostly soldiers. The fighting between Israel and the Iran-backed group has threatened to derail a US-Iran framework agreement calling for an end to military operations “on all fronts, including Lebanon.”
